questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
options: She has been working here since 2020.
She have been working here since 2020.
She has being working here since 2020.
questions.explanation: With 'since 2020', use the present perfect continuous: has/have been + verb-ing.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'Diligent':
questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking; 'industrious' is its closest synonym.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'Scarce':
questions.explanation: Scarce means rare or in short supply; its opposite is abundant (plentiful).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The committee ___ submitted its report.
questions.explanation: 'Committee' is treated as singular here, so it takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelled word:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is O-C-C-A-S-I-O-N.

questions.q: Find the error in: 'Neither of the two candidates are suitable.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so the verb must be 'is', not 'are'.

questions.q: The idiom 'to bite the dust' means:
questions.explanation: It comes from fallen riders in battle — it means to suffer defeat or failure.

questions.q: One word for 'a person who speaks many languages':
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows or uses several languages.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form of 'The manager approved the loan.':
options: The loan was approved by the manager.
The loan is approved by the manager.
The loan has approved by the manager.
The loan had approve by the manager.
questions.explanation: Past simple active becomes was/were + past participle in the passive voice.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'Frugal':
questions.explanation: Frugal means economical with money; its opposite is wasteful (extravagant).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition with 'good' (meaning skilled) is 'at'.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'Candid':
questions.explanation: Candid means frank, honest and outspoken.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: 'Hardly had he finished ___ the phone rang.'
questions.explanation: 'Hardly/Scarcely had' is always paired with 'when'.

questions.q: The word 'Benevolent' means:
questions.explanation: Benevolent describes someone kind, generous and well-meaning.

questions.q: Find the error in: 'She don't like tea.'
questions.explanation: With third-person singular 'she', the verb must be 'doesn't', not 'don't'.

questions.q: The idiom 'to break the ice' means:
questions.explanation: It means to do or say something to relieve tension and get people talking.

questions.q: What is the plural of 'Criterion'?
questions.explanation: 'Criterion' comes from Greek; its plural is 'criteria'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'Each of the students ___ a laptop.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has'.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'Adept':
questions.explanation: Adept means highly skilled or proficient at something.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'Expand':
questions.explanation: Expand means to grow larger; its opposite is contract (to shrink).

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles (×2 pattern), so 24 × 2 = 48.

questions.q: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Rose, Lotus and Marigold are flowers; Oak is a tree.

questions.q: If CAT = 24 (C=3, A=1, T=20, and 3+1+20 = 24), what is BAT?
questions.explanation: Add the letter positions: B(2) + A(1) + T(20) = 23.

questions.q: Statements: All banks are financial institutions. Some financial institutions are regulated by SBP. Which conclusion follows?
options: All banks are regulated by SBP
Some banks are regulated by SBP
No bank is regulated by SBP
No definite conclusion can be drawn
questions.explanation: The statements never link 'banks' to 'regulated', so nothing definite follows about banks.

questions.q: A is taller than B. B is taller than C. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: The order is A > B > C, so C is the shortest.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.explanation: The differences grow by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9…); the next difference is 11, so 26 + 11 = 37.

questions.q: If WATER = 67 (23+1+20+5+18), what is FIRE?
questions.explanation: Add the letter positions: F(6) + I(9) + R(18) + E(5) = 38.

questions.q: Which number does not belong? 121, 144, 169, 190
questions.explanation: 121 = 11², 144 = 12² and 169 = 13² are perfect squares; 190 is not.

questions.q: If yesterday was Friday, what day is the day after tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Today is Saturday and tomorrow is Sunday, so the day after tomorrow is Monday.

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: A, D, G, J, ?
questions.explanation: Each step moves three letters forward (+3): J + 3 = M.

questions.q: Statements: All managers are leaders. Some leaders are mentors. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The statements do not connect 'managers' to 'mentors', so nothing definite follows.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern is ×2 + 1: 47 × 2 + 1 = 95.

questions.q: Which one is different? Pen, Pencil, Eraser, Book
questions.explanation: Pen, pencil and eraser are writing instruments; a book is for reading.
Each number is multiplied by 3: 5 × 3 = 15.

questions.q: Ali walks 4 km north and then 3 km east. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: The two legs form a right triangle: √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 km.

questions.q: The State Bank of Pakistan was established in:
questions.explanation: The State Bank of Pakistan was established on 1 July 1948.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Zahid Hussain became the first Governor of SBP in 1948.

questions.q: The national currency of Pakistan is the:
questions.explanation: Pakistan's national currency is the Pakistani Rupee (PKR).

questions.q: Which is the largest dam in Pakistan by water storage capacity?
questions.explanation: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River has the largest live storage capacity in Pakistan.

questions.q: Which city of Pakistan is known as the 'City of Lights'?
questions.explanation: Karachi earned the title for its vibrant, never-sleeping nightlife.

questions.q: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in:
questions.explanation: Pakistan's nuclear tests (Youm-e-Takbeer) were conducted on 28 May 1998.

questions.q: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in:
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960.

questions.q: SAARC was founded in the year:
questions.explanation: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation was founded in Dhaka in 1985.

questions.q: The currency of Japan is the:
questions.explanation: The national currency of Japan is the Yen (¥).

questions.q: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about one-third of the Earth's surface.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in 1988 — the first woman to head a Muslim-majority country.

questions.q: The national animal of Pakistan is the:
questions.explanation: The Markhor, a wild goat of the northern mountains, is Pakistan's national animal.

questions.q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with:
questions.explanation: The historic Khyber Pass links Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Afghanistan.

questions.q: The United Nations was founded in:
questions.explanation: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars appears red because of iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

questions.q: The primary function of a central bank is to:
options: Issue currency and conduct monetary policy
questions.explanation: A central bank issues currency, sets monetary policy and regulates banks — it is not a commercial bank.

questions.q: When the State Bank raises its policy rate, borrowing in the economy becomes:
questions.explanation: A higher policy rate raises banks' funding costs, so loans become costlier — this cools down inflation.

questions.q: Inflation means:
options: A general rise in the price level
questions.explanation: Inflation is the sustained increase in the general price level, which reduces purchasing power.

questions.q: KIBOR stands for:
questions.explanation: KIBOR is the benchmark rate at which banks lend to each other in Pakistan.

questions.q: GDP stands for:
questions.explanation: GDP is the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year.

questions.q: An uncrossed (open) cheque can be encashed:
options: Only by the payee's own bank
questions.explanation: An open cheque is payable in cash across the counter; a crossed cheque must go through an account.

questions.q: The Banking Mohtasib in Pakistan deals with:
questions.explanation: The Banking Mohtasib is the ombudsman that resolves bank customers' complaints against banks.

questions.q: Which system provides instant digital payments in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: RAAST is SBP's instant payment system for real-time, low-cost digital transfers.

questions.q: In Pakistan, fiscal policy is formulated by:
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy — taxation and public spending — is the government's domain; SBP handles monetary policy.

questions.q: In banking, 'NPL' refers to:
questions.explanation: NPLs are loans on which borrowers have stopped paying — a key measure of a bank's health.
